tldr: LangChain's June newsletter previewed Deep Agents Rubrics and programmatic subagents as building blocks for its orchestration harness. On July 8, LangChain and NVIDIA turned that groundwork into a joint product: the NemoClaw Deep Agents blueprint pairing the harness with Nemotron 3 Ultra.
whats_new: LangChain and NVIDIA launched the NemoClaw Deep Agents blueprint, tuning LangChain's harness for Nemotron 3 Ultra with benchmark results claiming lower cost than top closed models.
why_it_matters: Platform engineers get a published, open reference stack — LangChain's harness plus open-weight Nemotron 3 Ultra and OpenShell — as an alternative to wiring a closed-model agent deployment from scratch.

status.detail: LangChain and NVIDIA launched the NemoClaw Deep Agents blueprint, pairing the Deep Agents harness with Nemotron 3 Ultra.

beats.headline: LangChain previews Deep Agents Rubrics and programmatic subagents
beats.summary: June newsletter lays groundwork for the harness: Fleet on-call copilot, Deep Agents Rubrics, and programmatic subagents.

beats.headline: LangChain and NVIDIA launch NemoClaw, pairing the Deep Agents harness with Nemotron 3 Ultra
beats.summary: NVIDIA publishes benchmark results and LangChain ships the blueprint combining Deep Agents Code, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and OpenShell for open, governed enterprise agents.

open_questions: Are the benchmark cost/performance numbers independently verified, or only NVIDIA's own comparison?
Does the NemoClaw blueprint require Nemotron 3 Ultra specifically, or does it generalize to other open-weight models?
Do Deep Agents Rubrics and programmatic subagents ship inside the NemoClaw blueprint, or remain separate LangSmith features?
take_for_builders: Evaluating open-weight agent stacks: pull the NemoClaw blueprint (LangChain Deep Agents harness + Nemotron 3 Ultra + OpenShell) as a reference before building a custom orchestration layer, and check NVIDIA's benchmark methodology before trusting the cost/performance claims.
